questions.prompt: A Layer 3 switch has routing enabled and an interface in each of two IP subnets. How does this differ from operating the same device only as a Layer 2 switch?

choices.text: It must stop using MAC addresses on Ethernet
choices.explanation: Routed Ethernet still uses link-layer headers.

choices.text: It can never forward frames within a VLAN
choices.explanation: Layer 2 switching and Layer 3 routing can coexist.

choices.text: It can forward packets between the configured IP networks
choices.explanation: The enabled routing function supplies inter-subnet forwarding.

choices.text: It automatically encrypts all routed packets
choices.explanation: Routing enablement does not imply encryption.

questions.explanation: A platform’s capabilities depend on its effective configuration. Enabling routing adds a Layer 3 function while Ethernet remains the link transport.

questions.prompt: The counters in the exhibit were cleared immediately before a 10-minute test. Duplex is verified full at both ends. What is the best next focus?

exhibit.content:
Operational duplex: full
Input packets: 180000
CRC errors: 430
Collisions: 0

choices.text: Change the subnet mask to remove CRC errors
choices.explanation: A mask change does not correct damaged Ethernet frames.

choices.text: Investigate physical-layer integrity and interface hardware
choices.explanation: New CRC errors justify cable, optic, connector, or hardware checks.

choices.text: Treat collisions as normal because the link is full duplex
choices.explanation: No collisions are shown, and full duplex does not use contention collisions.

choices.text: Conclude DNS is definitively the cause
choices.explanation: Frame error counters do not establish a DNS fault.

questions.explanation: Fresh CRC errors are link-integrity evidence. They do not by themselves prove which cable or hardware component is defective.

questions.prompt: An application sends two messages of 40 bytes each over one TCP connection. Which statement about receiver application reads is correct?

choices.text: Each read must return exactly one 40-byte message
choices.explanation: TCP does not preserve application message boundaries.

choices.text: TCP will combine the messages into one UDP datagram
choices.explanation: TCP does not change transport protocol in this way.

choices.explanation: ff identifies multicast, not anycast.

choices.explanation: Delivery is toward a selected instance, not all members.
